db_audit.slots: Two logical slots, BOTH temporary=t (session-bound, auto-dropped on owning-connection exit), two_phase=f, conflicting=f, no invalidation. (1) supabase_realtime_replication_slot_ — plugin wal2json, consumed by SQL polling, NOT via walsender (it has an active_pid backend but NO row in pg_stat_replication; it flickers active↔inactive between realtime.list_changes polls — observed active=t pid 929625 at 03:23, then inactive_since=03:24:48 one minute later). restart_lsn 34/E9002478, confirmed_flush 34/E9002B70 vs pg_current_wal_lsn 34/E9002B70 → restart lag 1784 bytes, confirmed lag 0 — fully caught up. wal_status=reserved, safe_wal_size≈528 MB (matches max_slot_wal_keep_size=512MB before invalidation). (2) supabase_realtime_messages_replication_slot_ — plugin pgoutput, real streaming walsender in pg_stat_replication: pid 1908, user supabase_admin, application_name realtime_replication_connection, client 172.18.0.13, state=streaming, sent/write/flush/replay all at head, backend_start 2026-07-08 05:16 (connection stable ~6 days). Same restart_lsn, lag ~0. GUCs: wal_level=logical, max_replication_slots=5 (2 used), max_wal_senders=10, max_slot_wal_keep_size=512MB, wal_keep_size=0, max_wal_size=8GB. The 61.4% list_changes cost is pure poll overhead (poll_interval_ms=100), not lag/backlog — both slots sit at the WAL head.
db_audit.retirement: What the rows show: _realtime.tenants has exactly one tenant (external_id 'realtime-dev', the self-host default) with postgres_cdc_default='postgres_cdc_rls', broadcast_adapter='gen_rpc', private_only=f, migrations_ran=72, feature_flags={}. _realtime.extensions has exactly ONE row: type='postgres_cdc_rls', tenant_external_id='realtime-dev', settings jsonb = {slot_name: "supabase_realtime_replication_slot" (Realtime appends the trailing '_'), publication: "supabase_realtime", poll_interval_ms: 100, poll_max_changes: 100, poll_max_record_bytes: 1048576, ssl_enforced: false, region: "us-east-1", db_host/db_name/db_port/db_user/db_password: redacted encrypted values} (inserted 2026-07-08 04:59). _realtime.feature_flags is empty. CONCLUSION FROM ROWS: the per-tenant enable switch for the wal2json poller is that single _realtime.extensions row of type postgres_cdc_rls — it names both the slot and the publication and carries the 100ms poll interval. Retiring the wal2json path = removing (or having Realtime's tenant API remove) that extensions row so the poller extension is not started for the tenant on the next Realtime boot. Slot lifecycle: pg_replication_slots.temporary=t proves Postgres itself drops the slot when the creating session disconnects (e.g. Realtime container stop); creation is therefore repeated by the consumer at startup — the DB rows show the poller's config names the slot, and a temporary slot cannot pre-exist its session, so the poller (for wal2json) and the walsender connection (for pgoutput/messages) each create their slot on connect. NOT determinable from the DB: whether Realtime v2 stops polling when realtime.subscription reaches zero rows without removing the extensions row, and whether the extensions row can be edited (e.g. poll_interval) rather than deleted — those are application (Elixir) behaviors with no trace in these tables. The pgoutput messages slot/extension row is separate and must be left untouched — broadcast (realtime.messages / gen_rpc) rides it.
risks: Stale-bundle behavior when dropping a table from the publication: the realtime.subscription rows for that table remain valid (entity is a regclass oid; ALTER PUBLICATION DROP TABLE does not touch them), so old frontend bundles keep a channel that reports SUBSCRIBED but silently receives no events — no error is surfaced at the DB layer. Whether Realtime v2 additionally rejects NEW joins for a non-published table is app behavior not visible in these rows. Safe order: ship the broadcast replacement first, wait for old bundles to age out (deploy pipeline flips a symlink — old tabs can hold stale JS indefinitely until reload), then drop the table from the publication, then remove the extensions row.

Do NOT drop the actual tables' publication membership by dropping/recreating the publication wholesale: supabase_realtime_messages_publication (realtime.messages_2026_07_11..17 partitions) is a separate publication feeding the broadcast slot — only ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime DROP TABLE ... on the wal2json one.

Both slots are TEMPORARY: any Realtime container restart drops both slots and they are recreated at the then-current LSN. Events written during Realtime downtime are permanently lost for BOTH postgres_changes and broadcast (realtime.send inserts into realtime.messages land fine but the recreated pgoutput slot starts past them). This is the existing delivery model, not a regression from W7 — but it means there is no replay safety net during the migration window.

Slot bloat is bounded, not unbounded: max_slot_wal_keep_size=512MB with wal_status=reserved and safe_wal_size≈528MB. If the poller stalls (e.g. Realtime wedged but session alive), WAL retention stops at ~512MB and the slot is invalidated rather than filling the disk. Current lag is ~0 bytes on both slots, so no retained-WAL problem exists today.

The list_changes cost (61.4% of DB time) will NOT drop by merely emptying the publication or losing all subscribers unless the poller itself stops: the extensions row hard-codes poll_interval_ms=100, and whatsapp-schema churn (1.28M writes vs 15k on published tables) dominates what wal2json must decode/skip each poll. Full retirement requires removing the postgres_cdc_rls extensions row (poller gone → temporary wal2json slot auto-dropped on session close), not just publication surgery.

3 published tables already have ZERO live subscribers right now (campaign_source_locks, courier_notifications, tracking_sync_runs) and near-zero churn — lowest-risk candidates to drop from the publication first; campaign_source_locks has literally never had a write on this box.
